hook.line: Everyone talks about vibe coding, but nobody shows the actual setup.
hook.visual: Phone filming a monitor that already shows the finished Claude Code panel in VS Code, with bold white captions with a red outline near the top.

beats.what: Finished Claude Code panel on screen while the hook is spoken: the end result first
Cut to the claude.ai sign-up page: step one, make an account and get Pro
Zoom punch into the sign-in box
Cut to the VS Code download site: step two
Cut to the VS Code welcome screen after install
Zoom punch toward the extensions sidebar icon
Camera moves onto the Claude Code extension page, pointing at about 5 million downloads and the Anthropic publisher
Cut with a larger caption 'ONCE THAT'S INSTALLED'
Claude Code panel open in VS Code, showing where you chat with it
Sign-in step, then the comment-'ready' ask over a live Claude reply

why_it_works: The finished setup is on screen during the hook, so beginners see where the steps lead
Numbered, one-action steps (account, VS Code, extension, sign in) make it feel easy and worth saving
Comment 'ready' CTA promises a part two, which drives comments and follows
Filming the monitor with a phone, with handheld moves and zoom punches, feels hands-on and not like a polished ad
weaknesses: No face at all (face_share 0), so there is no personal connection
Phone-filmed screen has moire and small UI text that is hard to read on a phone
Only 4 cuts in 63 s; long holds (up to 22.9 s) on static pages
Most text sits outside the safe zone (0.715)
for_robert: Show the finished result during the hook, then end with a comment-keyword ask for part two; Fred could hold up the keyword sign at the end.
